newsitem.title: USA: US March S&P 500s end strongly higher, near record.
newsitem.headline: US March S&P 500s end strongly higher, near record.

text.p: U.S. March Standard and Poor's 500 futures finished strongly higher and near another record as bullish technical momentum continued.
A late surge on Wednesday and again early Thursday in the technology sector quickly boosted S&Ps into uncharted territory, traders said.

March S&Ps wiped out bullish targets at 811.50, 813.10, 815.00 and 816.00, surging to record high 816.30 late in the session. Traders said the strong performance of Wednesday and Thursday puts March on track for bullish targets of 820.00 and 825.00.
Traders said a strong Treasury bond futures close helped boost March S&Ps to the most recent of a series of records, but small profit-taking near the S&P close limited gains.
Traders said three of four firms were sellers of 300 to 500 contracts each in March.
One trader noted "very average volume, nothing spectacular," in late trading. He said mild profittaking could hit March again on Friday, but overall the mood was still good.
"I don't see anything worrisome about this yet," he said.

On a five-minute chart of Thursday's action, the 810.00 level kept a floor under the market early and again after the 30-year bond auction. Traders said that level could now be support heading into the holiday weekend.
March S&Ps will have a regular trading session on Friday but will be closed on Monday for the Presidents' Day holiday. Other financial markets close early on Friday.
Treasury sold $10 billion of 30-year bonds at an average yield of 6.64 percent. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.42 and non-competitive bids totalled $318 million.
S&Ps paid little heed to an early mix of economic news.
U.S. January retail sales rose 0.6 percent overall and 0.4 percent excluding autos, both below forecasts. December sales were revised downward to a 0.3 percent gain.
The latest weekly jobless claims fell to 309,000 in the week ended February 8, down from a revised 324,000 the prior week.

Next up is January producer price data at 0730 CST/1330 GMT on Friday. Overall PPI is forecast up 0.3 percent and the core rate up 0.2 percent, versus December readings of up 0.5 percent and up 0.1 percent.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 6.90 points to 814.15, Value Lines were 2.95 higher at 717.15, NYSE Composites were 3.05 higher at 425.50, Nikkeis were 95 higher at 18,740, Midcap 400s were up 2.00 at 269.80 and Nasdaq 100s were up 2.00 at 908.75.
